title: Ledger reconciliation failure after cross-environment request routing
creator: Aisha Rahman
description: Several enterprise customers reported abrupt discrepancies on their invoices after a regional failover and a subsequent routing change that split traffic between Hosted and Dedicated stacks and backfilled to Private tenants. Symptoms included negative daily deltas in the customer ledger, transient credit reversals, and a recurring pattern of undercounted tokens for multi-hop requests. The issue triggered three escalations (one SEV2) and required urgent reconciliation to prevent billing errors and customer churn. This ticket tracks the investigation, immediate mitigations, root cause, and rollout of the permanent fix plus reconciliation tasks.
reproduction_steps: 1) Configure a test tenant that has cross-environment routing enabled (hosted->dedicated fallback->private) and enable streaming responses.
2) Send a burst of requests that triggers the retry middleware and force a regional failover mid-stream.
3) Observe ledger entries: verify undercount in primary ledger and duplicate negative adjustments in the reconciliation queue.
4) Capture traces spanning API gateway -> router -> dedicated pool -> private edge, and export token accounting events from metering-service for the same request IDs.
5) Reproduce consistent delta by toggling prefix/KV cache replay and request-id propagation flags.
root_cause: Race between retry/cache-replay logic and the request attribution layer during split-environment routing. When a request was proxied from Hosted to Dedicated and then re-routed to Private (failover), the request-id and attribution headers were not consistently propagated, causing metering-service to create duplicate accounting rows and to emit compensating negative adjustments later. In addition, an optimization in the token-aggregator assumed monotonic per-tenant updates and dropped late-arriving sub-second deltas, which left the ledger in an undercounted state while reconciliation emitted emergency credits incorrectly.
mitigation: 2025-03-05: Disabled cache-replay on failover paths for affected customers (temporary, gated by flag).
2025-03-06: Rolled out emergency guard in metering-service to coalesce duplicate request-ids within a 5s window to stop immediate double-counting.
2025-03-07: Added a manual reconciliation run for the three impacted customers and issued provisional billing credits while root cause investigation completed.
proposed_fix: 1) Harden request id propagation across all proxies and add explicit idempotency headers for metering events. 2) Update tokenizer-aggregator to accept and merge out-of-order sub-second deltas instead of dropping them. 3) Add an eventual-consistency reconciliation pass that deduplicates events based on composite keys (tenant_id, request_id, timestamp bucket) and emits a single canonical delta per logical request. 4) Add telemetry to detect split-route attribution gaps and surface them to Console dashboards.
plan: Week 1: Merge request-id propagation patch and deploy to staging; add unit/integration tests that simulate split routing.
Week 2: Deploy aggregator merge logic behind a feature flag to canary region; run synthetic traffic and monitor reconciler output.
Week 3: Enable production rollout to affected regions with observability checks and automatic rollback on abnormal deltas.
Post-rollout: Run full ledger reconciliation and backfill corrections; produce customer-facing report and finalize billing adjustments.
